summary: This Makefile snippet captures three pieces of information about the current Git repository: the branch name, the root directory path, and the repository URL. Each line runs a shell command and stores the result in a variable so it can be used later in build scripts or automation.

explanations.1: The $(shell ...) syntax tells Make to run a Git command and save its output. This particular command gets the current branch name you're on.
explanations.3: This runs a Git command to find the absolute path to the root folder of your repository, no matter which subfolder you're currently in.
explanations.5: This extracts the repository URL and transforms it from SSH format (git@github.com:user/repo.git) into HTTPS format (https://github.com/user/repo), then strips off the .git extension at the end using grep.
